transcript:
MEETING HEADER
Date: 2026-02-17
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 50 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood CSM); Lina (HelioGrid Eng Mgr), Tom (HelioGrid SRE), Priya (HelioGrid ML)

AUTO SUMMARY:
- Weekly pilot sync to review throughput experiments with continuous batching, concurrency targets, and queue shaping ("queueflow")
- Team observed 35% throughput uplift after enabling dynamic batch timeout and increasing concurrency; some OOMs traced to KV cache memory on a single worker
- Agreed next experiments: concurrency_target=28, batch_timeout_ms=12, prefix cache TTL tuning, 72-hr soak, and 1k prompt eval

TOPICS:
- Results from this week's load runs
- KV cache memory issue and shard sizing
- Concurrency vs batching tradeoffs
- Backpressure and graceful fallback to quantized model variant
- Plan and owners for next run

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Maya (AE): ok everyone thanks for joining, quick call today, like 45 minutes ish, we want to go over the numbers from the Friday runs and then set the next soak and action items.
[00:18] Lina (HelioGrid): yeah thanks, we had a couple late deploys so sorry, but we did pull the 2pm window tests and got some interesting graphs.
[00:30] Jonas (SE): cool, i'll share my screen in a sec, but high level: baseline without continuous batching we saw ~460 rps at target concurrency 16, with dynamic batch-timeout and the new queue shaping we peaked at ~620 rps steady state.
[00:45] Tom (SRE): to be precise, median latency p50 moved from 110ms to 125ms, p95 went 420ms to about 480ms during bursts, right? there was that p99 spike when one worker OOMed
[01:02] Jonas: yep that's right, the p95 bump was expected tradeoff as we favor larger batches to get token-efficiency. the p99 spike coincided with the kv cache module using more memory, look at worker-12 logs.
[01:20] Priya (ML Eng): can you say more about the KV cache thing? our prompts have variable seq lengths so maybe cache keys are larger than expected.
[01:30] Jonas: sure. we observed a hot-shard on worker-12 — the k v cache store was not sharded evenly because of the hashing skew with your userids. worker-12 hit the threshold and the runtime's allocator bumped memory causing OOM.
[01:45] Lina: ah that explains the one-off. are you recommending more shards or TTL changes?
[01:50] Jonas: two-pronged: increase shard_count from 16 to 32 for the pilot, and reduce prefix-cache TTL from 4h to 2h for the soak. that'll lower working set.
[02:05] Maya: ok that's feasible. also we thought about a backoff policy when a worker is close to mem threshold to fail-over to a smaller model variant (4-bit quantized) to preserve latency.
[02:20] Tom: is there an automatic fallback today? we don't want silent quality regressions though.
[02:26] Jonas: currently the routing layer can fallback to a compatible variant, but we need to wire a QoS check and an alert. fallback decision will log the model_id and reason for audit.
[02:40] Priya: can we tag the requests that used fallback so we can run evals on them later? quality monitoring tie-in?
[02:45] Jonas: absolutely, we'll add a header tag and a field in the trace. Redwood Console's eval hooks can pick those up.
[02:55] Maya: ok let's get into numbers. Jonas, can you run through the experiment table?
[03:00] Jonas: yes, so run A: concurrency 16, batch_timeout 20ms, cont-batching off — baseline 460 rps, cost est $32 per 100k tokens. Run B: concurrency 24, batch_timeout 14ms, cont-batching on — 580 rps, cost est $25 per 100k tokens. Run C: concurrency 32, batch_timeout 10ms, cont-batching on — hit 640 rps but with higher p99 and some tail latency and the OOM event.
[03:35] Lina: so middle ground looks good, 24 gave a good uplift without instability.
[03:40] Maya: how reproducible were those runs? ie, across three repeats were numbers stable?
[03:45] Jonas: B was stable across three repeats in the lab; C had two good repeats and one with the worker issue. Given the skew we saw I think it's safer to aim for concurrency_target=28 not full 32.
[03:58] Tom: what's the plan for request-rate shaping? we saw bursts from your replay around 09:15 that spiked the queue depth from 20 to 150 in 60s.
[04:10] Jonas: we propose a two-tier approach: soft admission control that caps active inflight at concurrency_target, plus queue shaping to spread arrivals using a small token-bucket on the edge. it smooths the bursts and lets batching assemble.
[04:30] Priya: that token bucket will add small delay, any estimate on added latency?
[04:35] Jonas: typically 5-15ms on average for 99% of requests — tradeoff for much larger batch sizes and token cost reduction.
[04:45] Lina: ok but we need to surface that in the SLA doc and also ensure developers see request-level attribution for when we throttle.
[04:55] Carlos (CSM): we can add trace flags and a dashboard tile that shows 'throttled vs served' counts per route.
[05:05] Maya: perfect. next, cost model — Priya, did you look at quality-vs-cost when fallback triggers?
[05:12] Priya: yes preliminary: fallback to 4-bit reduces token-cost by about 45% but model outputs degrade slightly on long-context summarization. we need to mark acceptable thresholds.
[05:25] Lina: for us, 2% quality regression in L2 metrics is ok, beyond that we want human review.
[05:32] Maya: noted. so experiments to run this week: concurrency_target 28, batch_timeout_ms 12, shard_count 32, prefix TTL 2h, enable soft admission + token-bucket. run for 72 hours.
[05:50] Jonas: i'll push the staging config today and run soak on staging then mirror to pilot infra for the 72-hr.
[05:58] Tom: i will provide the traffic replay file and the distribution by sequence length and user-id hashed — that should help you reproduce the hot shard.
[06:10] Lina: what metrics will we capture? we need p50/p95/p99, batch size distribution, cache hit ratio, worker mem footprints, and fallback counts.
[06:20] Jonas: yep we'll export all of those; also include token-cost per 100k tokens and an anomaly column for any OOMs.
[06:30] Maya: cool. any blockers from security/compliance side? we heard someone mention KMS rotation last week.
[06:36] Tom: KMS rotation scheduled next month; for pilot we are okay but we'll need the audit logs to include model routing events for SOC2 audit.
[06:45] Jonas: Redwood console can forward audit logs to your SIEM; we'll share the integration guide.
[06:52] Priya: one more thing — can we get a quick run with function-calling enabled? some of our prompts call external tools, curious about any latency impacts.
[07:00] Jonas: yes we can include a 30-minute run for function-call paths; they add about 30-50ms overhead depending on I/O.
[07:10] Maya: ok folks, last minute recap and owners.

RECAP / ACTIONS:
- Apply pilot config changes: concurrency_target=28, batch_timeout_ms=12, shard_count=32, prefix_cache_TTL=2h (Owner: Maya) due 2026-02-19
- Run 72-hour soak with traffic replay and collect p50/p95/p99, batch-size distribution, cache hit ratio, worker mem metrics, fallback counts (Owner: Jonas) due 2026-02-24
- Provide traffic replay and request distribution by length/user-id (Owner: Tom) due 2026-02-20
- Run 1k holdout prompt eval comparing fallback outputs and baseline (Owner: Priya) due 2026-02-22
- Share security/audit log integration doc and KMS rotation note (Owner: Maya/Carlos) due 2026-02-21
